text:
Ava: Heads up — saw a weird backlog in the us-west GPU pool for the last ~10m. Some jobs are holding whole cards and the rest of nodes are mostly idle :confused:
Sam: Which pool exactly? any job ids?
Ava: us-west-2-gpu-priority. I grabbed a snapshot of scheduler metrics: admit latency spiked and there are a couple of jobs pinned at head of their queue. gpu_util per node: [12%, 85%, 9%, 92%, 8%] — very uneven.
infra-bot: Alert: scheduler.queueing_delay > 30s for pool=us-west-2-gpu-priority at 1869001200.
Rohit: sounds like head-of-line blocking again. Did we roll the recent admission-window change?
Maya: We did a rollout last night (R: f2c9ab1) to change the admission smoothing window from 60s -> 180s.
Sam: That could make short jobs wait behind long ones. Can you paste the admission log for one of the stuck jobs?
Ava: paste logs:
```
I0318 11:20:12 admission_controller.go:214] admit: queue=low-prio job=job-9845 duration=0.002s
I0318 11:20:13 admission_controller.go:214] admit: queue=low-prio job=job-9846 duration=0.001s
I0318 11:22:30 admission_controller.go:540] enqueue: job=job-10001 reason=preemption_disabled
I0318 11:22:31 scheduler.go:778] dispatch: allocated node=node-34 job=job-10001 gpu=0
I0318 11:25:50 admission_controller.go:214] admit: queue=low-prio job=job-10002 duration=0.001s
```
Ava: Notice `preemption_disabled` for a long job at the front of queue. That prevented short jobs from being scheduled on idle GPUs.
Wei: Can reproduce locally with the new smoothing window + affinity packing. I ran `./bin/simulate --pattern=pack-heavy --window=180` and saw identical head-skipping behavior.
Rohit: OK produce hypothesis: the admission-window bumped aggregate token count per-queue, plus affinity packing is doing strict gang allocation, so a large gang blocks admission for subsequent smaller single-slot jobs even if other GPUs are free. Effectively head-of-line blocking due to mix of gang-affinity + longer smoothing.
Sam: Do we have any telemetry showing per-gpu pending allocations vs actual assignments?
Maya: yes — I pushed a dashboard under "Scheduler / Admission / Per-GPU Pending". It shows many GPUs with pending_allocations>0 but assigned_jobs=0 on some nodes.
Wei: Short-term mitigation: disable strict gang packing (`enable_strict_gang=false`) on us-west rollout and revert smoothing window to 60s for that pool.
Ava: Can we do a quick canary? change config for autoscaler group us-west-2-gpu-priority to `enable_strict_gang=false` and patch admission window back on private config.
Sam: I'll run the canary patch via the console: `kubectl -n infra set configmap scheduler-config --from-file=...` and set rollout to 10% nodes.
infra-bot: deploy-bot started rollout: configmap/scheduler-config -> us-west-2 (10% target).
Maya: After the canary I still see some idle GPUs but the pending queue clears much faster. admit latency dropped from ~80s -> ~5s on canary nodes.
Rohit: Good. We'll keep the canary for 30m and then either roll back the smoothing change or implement a fix that allows partial gang packing (allow smaller fillers) while preserving affinity.
Ava: Filing a short incident note and linking the PR that regressed rollout: https://git.internal/scheduler/pull/412
Sam: Also adding a unit test to simulate mixed gang+single workloads to catch this.
Wei: I'll capture pprof + nvml metrics from the affected nodes and upload to the incident thread.
Maya: FYI cost impact: inefficiency estimated ~2-3x token cost for that pool over the 10m window. We should include cost delta in the postmortem.
Rohit: Action items: (1) finish canary -> revert smoothing if stable (2) implement partial-fill fallback for gang allocations (3) add regression test + sim harness (4) postmortem with cost numbers.
Ava: thanks everyone — I'll coordinate the postmortem and tag eng-sre if anything persists. :thumbsup:
